items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Topics 8:1
items.html: Because they fell into the circle closest to the central point, where is the end of the illumination of the Makifim [surrounding lights] and the aspect of their empty void. And had they fallen further below — that is, further from the central point — then there the illumination of the Makifim is stronger, for in the circles there is no up and down, and their end is at their center. And the further one is from the center, the more important and the more illuminating it is. Therefore the vessels could not take the entire place of the direct light of the line, but only part of it — namely, the innermost circle, the one closest to the central point, which is the more dark. (Item 3).
